disclaimer: Education, not financial advice. Market values as at early November 2026.

scenes.headline: The 10 most valuable companies on earth
scenes.body: Nvidia. Apple. Microsoft. SpaceX. Aramco. And five more.
scenes.voiceover: Ten companies on earth are each worth more than one and a half trillion dollars.

scenes.headline: Together: about $30 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Together, they're worth about thirty trillion dollars. That's roughly ten times the size of Africa's entire economy. Here they are, counted down from ten to one.

scenes.headline: By market value: share price × shares.
scenes.body: Values as at early November 2026. They move every day.
scenes.voiceover: We ranked them by market value, which is the share price multiplied by the number of shares. These figures are from early November twenty twenty-six, and they change every day. For each one: where it's based, who founded it, what it does, and what it's known for.

scenes.headline: Broadcom
scenes.voiceover: Number ten. Broadcom. Based in Palo Alto, in the United States.

scenes.name: Broadcom
scenes.headline: Worth about $1.57 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about one point five seven trillion dollars.

scenes.name: Broadcom
scenes.headline: 1961 roots in HP. Broadcom name from 1991.
scenes.voiceover: Its roots go back to Hewlett-Packard's chip division in nineteen sixty-one, which became Avago. The Broadcom name comes from a company Henry Samueli and Henry Nicholas founded in nineteen ninety-one. Avago bought it in twenty sixteen and took the name.

scenes.name: Broadcom
scenes.headline: Chips and software for data centres
scenes.voiceover: Broadcom designs the networking and custom AI chips inside the world's data centres, and since buying VMware it's also a major software company. It does all this with about thirty-three thousand employees.

scenes.headline: The quiet giant of AI
scenes.body: It helps big tech firms design their own AI chips.
scenes.voiceover: Most people have never heard of Broadcom, yet it helps companies like Google build their own artificial intelligence chips. That's why its value has soared.

scenes.headline: Meta Platforms
scenes.voiceover: Number nine. Meta Platforms. Based in Menlo Park, in the United States.

scenes.name: Meta Platforms
scenes.headline: Worth about $1.6 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about one point six trillion dollars.

scenes.name: Meta Platforms
scenes.headline: 2004: Mark Zuckerberg and four Harvard roommates
scenes.voiceover: Mark Zuckerberg started Facebook in two thousand and four from his Harvard dorm room, with Eduardo Saverin, Andrew McCollum, Dustin Moskovitz and Chris Hughes. The company renamed itself Meta in twenty twenty-one.

scenes.name: Meta Platforms
scenes.headline: Social media and online advertising
scenes.voiceover: Meta owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads, and makes almost all of its money from advertising. It employs just under seventy-nine thousand people.

scenes.headline: Over 3.5 billion people a day
scenes.body: Use at least one Meta app daily, including WhatsApp.
scenes.voiceover: More than three and a half billion people use at least one of its apps every single day. If you've sent a WhatsApp today, you're one of them.

scenes.headline: Saudi Aramco
scenes.voiceover: Number eight. Saudi Aramco. Based in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia.

scenes.name: Saudi Aramco
scenes.headline: Worth about $1.65 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about one point six five trillion dollars.

scenes.name: Saudi Aramco
scenes.headline: 1933 oil concession. Fully Saudi-owned by 1980.
scenes.voiceover: Aramco began in nineteen thirty-three, when the Saudi government granted an oil concession to an American company, Standard Oil of California. The Saudi state took full ownership by nineteen eighty.

scenes.name: Saudi Aramco
scenes.headline: Oil and gas
scenes.voiceover: It's the world's biggest oil producer, and for years one of the most profitable companies on earth. The Saudi government still owns the vast majority of it. Aramco employs more than seventy-five thousand people from over ninety nationalities.

scenes.headline: The only non-tech giant in the top 10
scenes.body: Its 2019 listing was the world's biggest, until SpaceX.
scenes.voiceover: It's the only company in the top ten that isn't a technology business. Its twenty nineteen stock market listing was the biggest in history, until this year.

scenes.headline: TSMC
scenes.voiceover: Number seven. T S M C. Based in Hsinchu, Taiwan.

scenes.name: TSMC
scenes.headline: Worth about $1.9 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about one point nine trillion dollars.

scenes.name: TSMC
scenes.headline: 1987: Morris Chang
scenes.voiceover: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company was founded in nineteen eighty-seven by Morris Chang, with backing from the Taiwanese government.

scenes.name: TSMC
scenes.headline: Making chips for other companies
scenes.voiceover: TSMC doesn't sell its own brand. It manufactures chips designed by others, including Apple and Nvidia. It has nearly eighty-four thousand employees.

scenes.headline: The factory behind your phone
scenes.body: It makes most of the world's most advanced chips.
scenes.voiceover: The chip in your phone was very likely made by TSMC. It makes most of the world's most advanced processors, which is why it matters so much to global politics.

scenes.headline: SpaceX
scenes.voiceover: Number six. SpaceX. Based in Starbase, Texas, in the United States.

scenes.name: SpaceX
scenes.headline: Worth about $2 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about two trillion dollars.

scenes.name: SpaceX
scenes.headline: 2002: Elon Musk
scenes.voiceover: Elon Musk founded Space Exploration Technologies in two thousand and two, with the goal of cutting the cost of getting to space.

scenes.name: SpaceX
scenes.headline: Rockets and satellite internet
scenes.voiceover: SpaceX launches most of the world's rockets, and its Starlink satellites now sell internet to more than twelve million customers in over a hundred and sixty countries. It has more than twenty-two thousand employees.

scenes.headline: The biggest stock market listing ever
scenes.body: It listed on Nasdaq in June 2026, valued at about $2 trillion.
scenes.voiceover: SpaceX only joined the stock market in June twenty twenty-six, in the biggest listing in history. It went straight into the top ten.

scenes.headline: Amazon
scenes.voiceover: Number five. Amazon. Based in Seattle, in the United States.

scenes.name: Amazon
scenes.headline: Worth about $2.7 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about two point seven trillion dollars.

scenes.name: Amazon
scenes.headline: 1994: Jeff Bezos, in a garage
scenes.voiceover: Jeff Bezos founded Amazon in nineteen ninety-four, in a garage outside Seattle, as an online bookshop.

scenes.name: Amazon
scenes.headline: Online shopping and cloud computing
scenes.voiceover: Amazon is the world's biggest online store, but most of its profit comes from Amazon Web Services, the cloud computers that run much of the internet. It employs about one point five eight million people, more than any other company on this list.

scenes.headline: Now shipping in South Africa
scenes.voiceover: And it's close to home. Amazon launched its South African store in twenty twenty-four, and its cloud has run a data centre region in Cape Town since twenty twenty.

scenes.headline: Alphabet
scenes.voiceover: Number four. Alphabet. Based in Mountain View, in the United States.

scenes.name: Alphabet
scenes.headline: Worth about $3.9 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about three point nine trillion dollars.

scenes.name: Alphabet
scenes.headline: 1998: Larry Page and Sergey Brin
scenes.voiceover: Larry Page and Sergey Brin founded Google in nineteen ninety-eight, while they were PhD students at Stanford. Alphabet was created in twenty fifteen as the parent company.

scenes.name: Alphabet
scenes.headline: Search, advertising, YouTube and cloud
scenes.voiceover: Alphabet owns Google Search, Android, Google Cloud, and YouTube, and it earns most of its money from advertising. It has around one hundred and ninety thousand employees.

scenes.headline: You're on its platform right now
scenes.voiceover: And if you're watching this on YouTube, you're using one of its products right now. Google bought YouTube in two thousand and six.

scenes.headline: Microsoft
scenes.voiceover: Number three. Microsoft. Based in Redmond, in the United States.

scenes.name: Microsoft
scenes.headline: Worth about $4 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about four trillion dollars.

scenes.name: Microsoft
scenes.headline: 1975: Bill Gates and Paul Allen
scenes.voiceover: Childhood friends Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft in nineteen seventy-five.

scenes.name: Microsoft
scenes.headline: Software and cloud computing
scenes.voiceover: Microsoft makes Windows and Office, and runs Azure, one of the world's biggest cloud platforms. It's also a major investor in OpenAI. It employs about two hundred and twenty-three thousand people.

scenes.headline: On almost every office computer
scenes.body: Its products are sold in more than 190 countries.
scenes.voiceover: Its software runs on almost every office computer in the world, and it sells in more than one hundred and ninety countries.

scenes.headline: Apple
scenes.voiceover: Number two. Apple. Based in Cupertino, in the United States.

scenes.name: Apple
scenes.headline: Worth about $5 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about five trillion dollars.

scenes.name: Apple
scenes.headline: 1976: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, Ronald Wayne
scenes.voiceover: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne founded Apple in nineteen seventy-six. Wayne sold his ten percent share just days later, for eight hundred dollars.

scenes.name: Apple
scenes.headline: Phones, computers and services
scenes.voiceover: Apple makes the iPhone, Mac, iPad and Apple Watch, and earns a fast-growing share of its money from services like the App Store and iCloud. It has about one hundred and sixty-six thousand employees.

scenes.headline: First to a trillion dollars
scenes.body: The first US company worth $1 trillion, in 2018.
scenes.voiceover: Apple was the first American company to be worth a trillion dollars, in twenty eighteen. It and Nvidia now swap the number one spot almost week to week.

scenes.headline: Nvidia
scenes.voiceover: Number one. Nvidia. Based in Santa Clara, in the United States.

scenes.name: Nvidia
scenes.headline: Worth about $5.2 trillion
scenes.voiceover: Market value: about five point two trillion dollars.

scenes.name: Nvidia
scenes.headline: 1993: Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, Curtis Priem
scenes.voiceover: Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem founded Nvidia in nineteen ninety-three. They planned it over meals at a roadside diner.

scenes.name: Nvidia
scenes.headline: Chips that power artificial intelligence
scenes.voiceover: Nvidia started out making graphics chips for video games. Today its processors power most of the world's artificial intelligence. It has about forty-two thousand employees in thirty-eight countries.

scenes.headline: First company worth $5 trillion
scenes.voiceover: In October twenty twenty-five, Nvidia became the first company ever worth five trillion dollars. That's about twelve times the size of South Africa's entire economy.

scenes.headline: Eight of the ten are American tech companies.
scenes.voiceover: Notice the pattern. Eight of the ten are American, and nine of them are technology businesses. The only oil company left is Aramco. Twenty years ago, this list was full of oil companies and banks.

scenes.headline: Tesla, Eli Lilly and Berkshire Hathaway
scenes.voiceover: Just missing out: Tesla, only a few billion dollars behind Broadcom, followed by Eli Lilly and Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway. With prices moving every day, this list could look different by next month.

scenes.headline: Which company will be number one next year?
scenes.voiceover: So which company do you think will be number one this time next year? Tell us in the comments.

The 10 most valuable companies in the world by market value, as at early November 2026: where they're based, who founded them, what they do, how many people they employ, and what they're known for. Nvidia alone is worth about 12 times South Africa's economy.

{chapters}

Sources: market values from TradingView (early November 2026); employee numbers from each company's latest annual report; South Africa GDP from Trading Economics / World Bank (2025).

Education, not financial advice. Narration and some visuals are AI-generated. Stock footage from Pexels.
